chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ribi'i ibn 'Abdullah and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of the Exalted
"And whoever's provision is restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him."
He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he spends on her what sustains her back (i.e., supports her adequately) along with clothing, then [the marriage continues]; otherwise, they are separated.'

key_terms.يُقِيمُ صُلْبَهَا: Sustains her back (idiom for adequate support/maintenance)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes sufficient spending (nafaqah) for a wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'spending' (infaq) is specifically defined as providing sufficient maintenance (nafaqah) to sustain the wife's physical well-being and clothing. The Imam clarifies that if the husband cannot afford this basic standard of living, the obligation shifts to separation (talaq), establishing a practical limit to financial responsibility based on capacity. This interpretation underscores the Shia juristic principle that nafaqah is tied to the wife's actual needs rather than a fixed arbitrary amount.
